paper.title: Codes, Patterns and Shapes of Contemporary Online Antisemitism and Conspiracy Narratives - an Annotation Guide and Labeled German-Language Dataset in the Context of COVID-19

collection.scale_description_verbatim: 3,663 messages from 133 public German-language Telegram channels

tasks_verbatim: validate existing approaches to detecting conspiracy theories, antisemitic speech
annotation_paradigms: Expert, author or trained student annotation
annotation.iaa_summary_verbatim: Our results indicate solid agreement among annotators, with Cohen’s kappa being 0.7 for conspiracy theory and 0.84 for antisemitism.

ethics.anonymization_details: User names, user IDs, and links to those identifiers were replaced with USER before release.

evidence.availability_quote: Furthermore we decided only to provide our annotated dataset on personal request for research purposes approved for our ethical standards, thereby preventing any attempt of abuse.
evidence.scale_quote: After this step, another random sample was drawn and annotated, resulting in the final dataset TelCovACT containing 3,663 messages from public German-language Telegram channels in the time period between March 11, 2020 and December 19, 2021.
evidence.annotation_quote: Our annotation scheme is based on the working definitions of antisemitism and conspiracy theories presented above, and extended by sub-labels to specify the stance and content of a given instance. All instances in the dataset are annotated by two annotators.
evidence.ethics_quote: Even though Telegram’s Terms of Service states that user names and ids cannot be linked to a user’s phone number as the only personal data collected by Telegram, we chose to additionally anonymize the dataset by replacing user names, user-ids as well as links to such by USER.
evidence.ambiguity_notes: The abstract gives an approximate size of ∼3,700, while the corpus description reports the exact total of 3,663. The annotation team comprised nine individuals, with two annotators per message; Cohen’s kappa is reported separately as 0.7 for conspiracy theory and 0.84 for antisemitism.
